name: Itza' Maya
summary: Conjugate verbs with aspects and person markers, and see how they change in the past.

conjugator.label: Verb
conjugator.hint: Type the verb as in the dictionary: wenel «sleep» (intransitive) or ilik «see» (transitive).

own.hint: Type any verb and its meaning in English. If you choose its type, you can type just the root (wen, il, meyaj).
own.label: Verb or root
own.types_help: If you type the dictionary form (wenel, ilik, jantik), we detect it ourselves.

source.full: Charles Andrew Hofling with Fernando Tesucún. Itzaj Maya Grammar. University of Utah Press, 2000. Examples also from Jiilt'an Maya Itza: Vocabulario Itza' (Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala, 2001).

about: Itza' is a Mayan language of the Yucatecan branch, related to Yucatec Maya, Mopan and Lacandon. It is spoken in San José, Petén, on the shore of Lake Petén Itzá, in Guatemala.
The Itza' ruled the last independent Maya kingdom: its capital, Noj Petén, held out against the Spanish until 1697.

Today the language is severely endangered: in the late 1990s only a few dozen elders spoke it as their first language. The community of San José and the Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala are working to revitalize it.

orthography.intro: This is the spelling of the Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala, with ts and ts' for the affricates. The apostrophe (') marks a glottalized consonant (k', t') or a glottal stop, a short break in the voice.
notes: A vowel can have a glottal stop in the middle: kan «snake», ka'an «sky». Ä is always short.
Long vowels are not written: a single vowel is written.
R appears mostly in words that come from Spanish, like riyoj «river».
Pronunciation is shown in brackets with the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA).

grammar.intro: An Itza' verb is built from pieces: sometimes an auxiliary word, an aspect marker, a person prefix, the verb and a status suffix. To look up a verb, type it as in the dictionary: wenel «sleep», ilik «see».

items.description: Optional word that adds a meaning: k'ab'et «need», tak «want».
When or how the action happens: k- habit, tan now.
Suffix that changes with the aspect: -el, -ik, -aj…

blocks.title: Two sets of person markers
blocks.description: Set A goes before the verb; set B, after it. Before a vowel, set A adds w or y: in-w-il, u-y-il.
blocks.note: «We» with -e'ex at the end includes the listener: kiwenele'ex «we all sleep».

blocks.title: In the past, the person moves
blocks.description: In the present, set A marks who does the action in every verb. In the past, intransitive verbs use set B at the end.

items.name: Intransitive
items.description: No object. Its suffix repeats the vowel of the root: wen-el, jok'-ol, nak'-äl.

items.name: Root transitive
items.description: Takes an object. In the past it takes t- and -aj.

items.name: Transitive with -t
items.description: The -t- makes transitive verbs. In the perfect the -t- changes to -m-.

blocks.title: Auxiliary words
blocks.description: They come before the verb, which keeps its person prefix and its -Vl or -ik suffix, without k-.

blocks.title: The moods: dependent status
blocks.description: For what isn't real yet (wishes, orders, warnings), the verb takes the dependent status: -Vk in intransitive verbs and -V' or -ej in transitive ones.

items.name: Subjunctive
items.description: «That…»: what may or may not happen.

items.name: Imperative
items.description: Orders. In the negative, ma' is used with the present.

items.name: Warning
items.description: Warns about something that could happen.

blocks.title: Negation: ma'
blocks.description: To negate the present, tan is used, the marker of what is happening.

tenses.name: Habitual present
tenses.description: What always happens, or by habit (k-).

tenses.name: Near future
tenses.description: What you are about to go and do (ka'aj, «go to»).

tenses.name: Subjunctive
tenses.description: What may or may not happen: «that…» (ka').

tenses.name: Imperative
tenses.description: To say «don't do it»: ma' + a-.

lexicon.note: Irregular: b'el, past b'in, subjunctive xi'ik, imperative xen
